text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall — elevated 5xx rate and routing errors for eu-west-1 observed across multiple customers. Auto-alert at 1747999987; creating thread for live mitigation and RCA coordination.

maria: I’m on it. grabbing logs and will collect a timeline. can someone confirm if any routing changes were pushed in the last 30m?

jon: I didn't push anything. I saw a config PR merged ~18m ago by alex that touched routing policy service. cc @alex

alex: that was a small change to tier fallback order for canary routing (move tier-b fallback before tier-c) — meant to lower cost for non-critical traffic. I backfilled the PR link here: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/4521

lee: ok that matches the spike time. symptoms: increased latency, then a flood of 502/503 from model proxies in eu-west-1, then regional spillover to us-west-2. customers reporting degraded responses and timeouts.

maria: building timeline now. posting notable events we see from metrics and deploy history: 
- 1747999900: traffic steady.
- 1747999987: alert triggered on rising 5xx rate.
- 1748000000: alex merged PR 4521 to routing-service.
- 1748000035: spike in proxy error logs in eu-west-1.
- 1748000102: auto-fallback policy engaged; traffic routed to cheaper model variant in eu-west-1 (tier-b).
- 1748000170: tier-b instances in eu-west-1 started returning 503s under load.
- 1748000205: smart-router began spilling traffic to us-west-2.
- 1748000300: ops mitigation: pause rollout + force route to dedicated pool in eu-west-1.

jon: sharing quick grep of proxy logs around spike (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T12:20:35Z proxy[euw-01] ERROR upstream=kv-cache timeout model=redwood-small v=2026-03-15-12:20:33
2026-03-15T12:20:36Z proxy[euw-01] WARN routing: fallback_attempt tier=b route_policy=canary id=ms-xyz
2026-03-15T12:20:40Z proxy[euw-01] ERROR upstream=backend-503 model=redwood-small code=503
```

alex: from routing-service logs (relevant lines):
```
2026-03-15T12:19:58Z routing-service INFO apply_policy policy=canary user_requests=1200
2026-03-15T12:20:00Z routing-service DEBUG evaluate_fallback order=[tier-a,tier-b,tier-c]
2026-03-15T12:20:01Z routing-service INFO override_order -> [tier-a,tier-b,tier-c] (applied change from PR 4521)
2026-03-15T12:20:34Z routing-service WARN selected=tier-b target_pool=eu-west-1-tier-b
```

maria: hypothesis tracker (in-thread):
- H1: PR 4521 changed fallback order causing higher load on tier-b models in eu-west-1, which are smaller/less provisioned and hit capacity -> 503s.
- H2: A separate regression in tier-b model deployment reduced capacity (e.g., bad image), coincidentally aligned with PR change.
- H3: Smart-router miscalculated permissive spillover thresholds and spilled too early to us-west-2, amplifying cross-region latency.

lee: quick check: use this runbook command to inspect pool utilization and active containers in eu-west-1 (run in prod-readonly):
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=eu-west-1-tier-b -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
kubectl -n inference top pods -l pool=eu-west-1-tier-b
```

jon: I ran them — tier-b shows 70% of pods OOM/crashloop on that revision. image tag `redwood/model:v2-small-20260312` has elevated restarts. Logs show `OOMKilled` and `failed to allocate kv cache`.

alex: that explains capacity reduction. PR 4521 changed fallback order which routed more traffic to tier-b *and* tier-b was already degraded. Nasty two-factor.

maria: mitigation steps taken so far (chronological):
1) 1748000301 — paused routing-service rollout (reverted PR 4521).
2) 1748000320 — pin traffic for high-tier customers to tier-a/dedicated pools (manual override).
3) 1748000355 — scale-up of eu-west-1 tier-b attempted but pods kept crashing.
4) 1748000380 — emergency migration of critical traffic to us-east-1 dedicated pool for affected customers.

ops-runner-bot: Note: sent customer-impact emails to customers A,B,C at 1748000405.

lee: immediate asks to close this incident:
- Confirm revert of PR 4521 persisted and no further canary rollouts are active.
- Roll back problematic tier-b image or mark it unhealthy so routing won't select it.
- Tune spillover threshold to avoid region cascade.
- Postmortem: timeline + root cause + follow-ups.

jon: I pushed image-mark for `redwood/model:v2-small-20260312` -> `unhealthy` in the image registry so autoscaler won't schedule it. PR to revert image is here: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/4523

alex: I initiated a hotfix to revert fallback order and redeployed routing-service config to the previous stable snapshot at 1747999600. Confirmed no further changes in the pipeline.

maria: live actions assigned:
- alex: ensure routing-service config is fully reverted and add a safety gate so fallback changes require a 30m gradual canary and explicit capacity check.
- jon: coordinate image rollback for tier-b and watch pod health.
- lee: investigate spillover thresholds and propose a small tweak to the hysteresis logic to reduce cross-region cascade risk.
- maria: draft incident summary and collect logs for RCA.

alex: note for the RCA: fallback order changes need a canary that simulates load for each affected pool. I'll add a gate in the config service.

jon: hypothesis validation evidence we have so far:
- evidence for H1: timing of PR + routing-service `selected=tier-b` + spike in tier-b traffic.
- evidence for H2: OOM/crashloop in tier-b pods — shows capacity regression unrelated to routing change.
- evidence for H3: smart-router spillover logs show early-triggering threshold at 12s latency. Need to correlate with recent tuning commit by infra.

maria: quick customer-impact notes (to include in RCA):
- ~15% of requests for paid customers A,B,C saw elevated latency or 5xx between 1747999987 and 1748000355.
- No data exfiltration or PII exposure.
- Support tickets created: #7891, #7892.

lee: suggested immediate post-incident follow-ups (owners):
- Upgrade tier-b instances with larger kv-cache config (owner: infra-team).
- Add routing-service pre-check that queries target pool health before applying fallback reorders (owner: alex).
- Add automatic image health gating to prevent scheduling known-crashy image (owner: jon).
- Update playbook for region spillover mitigation with explicit step to pause cross-region spill for 5m after detection (owner: maria).

maria: recording action items into the incident tracker now. will produce a draft RCA skeleton and share here in ~30m. please paste any missing logs or screens.

alex: pasting small snippet of routing policy code that caused the issue (sanitized):
```
// old fallback: [tier-a, tier-c, tier-b]
// new fallback (PR 4521): [tier-a, tier-b, tier-c]
if (!pool_healthy(tier_a)) return fallback_to(tier_b);
```

jon: adding grep for smart-router spill events to correlate thresholds:
```
grep -R "spillover" /var/log/smart-router/ | tail -n 200
2026-03-15T12:20:21Z smart-router INFO spillover reason=latency region=euw-1 threshold_ms=12000
2026-03-15T12:20:25Z smart-router INFO spillover action=reroute target=us-west-2
```

maria: good. Let's keep this thread as the single source-of-truth for the in-incident RCA artifacts. When we have the full timeline and logs, we'll convert to the formal postmortem template.

ops-runner-bot: Reminder: please add the oncall handoff note if you hand off before closure.

lee: I’m taking first post-incident writeup for the RCA (will include timeline, hypotheses, evidence, and remediation). If someone takes handoff later, add their notes.

maria: closing live mitigation portion: incident declared resolved at 1748000410 after revert + image mark and temporary routing overrides. creating post-incident ticket: INC-2026-037.

jon: leaving logs I pulled into the incident S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-037/logs/1748000000-1748000410.tar.gz

alex: will author the config-service PR to add canary and capacity check (ETA: 48h).

maria: thanks all. continuing RCA in this thread; please append any additional traces or customer notes.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-037: status=resolved severity=sev2 duration=~7m actions=[revert-routing, mark-bad-image, reroute-critical].
